Topology Spread Constraints (`topologySpreadConstraints`) ensure pods are distributed evenly across availability zones.
Pod Disruption Budgets (`minAvailable: 2`) prevent voluntary evictions from taking down active SSE streaming capacity.

research_clusters.name: Cluster 2: Custom Metrics Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (HPA)

rounds.topic: Standard CPU/memory metrics fail to reflect true l
rounds.finding: Standard CPU/memory metrics fail to reflect true load on streaming SSE connections with low compute utilization.

rounds.topic: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA v2) scales on custo
rounds.finding: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA v2) scales on custom Prometheus metrics via the Prometheus Adapter or KEDA.
Primary scaling metric: `mcp_active_sse_connections` per pod (target: 2,500 active connections per pod).
Secondary scaling metric: `mcp_tool_execution_queue_depth` (triggers scaling when worker channels are >70% full).
Scale-up behavior: instantaneous aggressive scaling (double pod count within 15 seconds) to absorb traffic surges.
Scale-down behavior: gradual stabilization window (300 seconds) to prevent pod churn during transient traffic dips.

rounds.topic: Cluster Autoscaler adds bare-metal Kubernetes work
rounds.finding: Cluster Autoscaler adds bare-metal Kubernetes worker nodes when pod scheduling requests exceed cluster capacity.
KEDA (Kubernetes Event-driven Autoscaling) integrates directly with Redis queue depths for asynchronous tool processing.
Benchmarking autoscaling response: cluster scales from 4 to 24 pods in 45 seconds under simulated 500% load spike.
Cost optimization: scheduled scaling downscales staging environments during off-business hours, saving 65% compute.

research_clusters.name: Cluster 5: Semantic Versioning & Non-Breaking Schema Evolution

rounds.topic: Updating tool parameters in production can break d
rounds.finding: Updating tool parameters in production can break deployed autonomous agents that rely on specific schema structures.

rounds.topic: Semantic Versioning (SemVer 2.0) rules are strictly enforced on all MCP tool definitions
rounds.finding: Semantic Versioning (SemVer 2.0) rules are strictly enforced on all MCP tool definitions: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.
PATCH updates: internal bug fixes, performance optimizations, and documentation clarifications with zero schema change.
MINOR updates: adding new optional parameters with sensible defaults, or adding new tools to an existing server.
MAJOR updates: removing parameters, changing parameter types, or altering tool semantic behavior.

rounds.topic: Deprecation headers on JSON-RPC responses alert cl

rounds.topic: Client telemetry tracking monitors migration progr

research_clusters.name: Cluster 9: Incident Response, Runbooks & SRE Operational Playbooks

rounds.finding: Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) teams maintain detailed operational runbooks for all MCP production failure scenarios.
Runbook 01: Downstream Database Connection Pool Exhaustion — diagnostic commands, temporary pool resizing, kill slow queries.
Runbook 02: Runaway Agent Loop Mitigation — session identification, circuit breaker tripping, agent credential revocation.
Runbook 03: Sudden P99 Latency Degradation — trace analysis, identifying bottleneck microservice, cache warming.
Runbook 04: SSL/TLS Certificate Expiration — SPIRE root rotation, manual emergency certificate issuance, gateway restart.
Runbook 05: Poisoned Tool Ingestion — registry rollback, cache purging, affected session identification and notification.
Automated alert escalation: PagerDuty routes alerts to on-call platform engineers based on service ownership metadata.
